name: Instagram
description: Design Instagram's photo/video sharing platform. Covers media upload pipeline, news feed generation, CDN delivery, and social graph interactions at scale.

chaosScenarios.name: Feed Cache Cluster Failure
chaosScenarios.description: Redis cluster holding precomputed user timelines fails; all feed reads fall through to PostgreSQL
chaosScenarios.expectedBehavior: Feed p99 climbs from ~150ms to multi-second as feed-service recomputes timelines from the Post DB. DB read IOPS spike 10x; recompute storms threaten to take the database down with the cache. Some users see stale or truncated feeds.
mitigationSteps: Switch feed-service to degraded chronological reads from DB with strict row limits
Enable per-user recompute rate limiting to protect PostgreSQL
Rebuild the Redis cluster and warm timelines for the most active users first
Verify hit rate > 80% before disabling degraded mode

chaosScenarios.name: CDN Cache Flush / POP Outage
chaosScenarios.description: A regional CDN POP outage or mass cache eviction sends media requests straight to the S3 origin
chaosScenarios.expectedBehavior: Origin egress jumps 20x. S3 returns 503 SlowDown on hot prefixes; media time-to-first-byte degrades from ~50ms to 500ms+. App tier is unaffected since media bypasses it entirely.
mitigationSteps: Enable origin shield / tiered caching to coalesce origin fetches
Raise cache TTLs on hot media objects
Verify S3 SlowDown rate is subsiding as the cache refills
Coordinate with CDN vendor on POP status and traffic steering

chaosScenarios.name: Event Bus Fan-out Lag
chaosScenarios.description: Kafka partition leader loss plus consumer lag delays fan-out of new posts into follower feeds
chaosScenarios.expectedBehavior: Posting succeeds (write path is healthy) but new posts take minutes instead of seconds to appear in follower feeds. No user-visible errors — only freshness degrades, so the issue surfaces via lag metrics, not error rates.
mitigationSteps: Scale the feed-service consumer group to drain lag
Switch highest-follower accounts to pull-based merge while lag persists
Backfill missed posts from the Post DB by timestamp once lag clears

bottleneckProgression.description: Post metadata and social graph queries saturate the PostgreSQL connection pool
bottleneckProgression.resolution: Add read replicas, route reads through PgBouncer, and cache social graph edges

bottleneckProgression.description: Feed cache eviction churn — per-user timelines exceed cluster memory and hit rate drops
bottleneckProgression.resolution: Shard the Redis cluster, cap timeline length per user, and compress entries

bottleneckProgression.description: API gateway CPU saturates on TLS termination, auth, and routing at peak
bottleneckProgression.resolution: Scale gateways horizontally and deploy regional gateway pools

expectedIssues.title: Celebrity Fan-out Explosion
expectedIssues.description: A post from an account with 100M followers requires 100M timeline writes; push fan-out floods Kafka and the feed cache
expectedIssues.mitigation: Hybrid push/pull — fan-out on write for normal accounts, pull-and-merge at read time for high-follower accounts

expectedIssues.title: Viral Media Hot Object
expectedIssues.description: A viral Reel concentrates millions of requests on one CDN object and a single S3 key prefix
expectedIssues.mitigation: Replicate hot objects across POPs, randomize S3 key prefixes, serve multiple renditions to spread load

expectedIssues.title: Deleted Content Lingers in Cached Feeds
expectedIssues.description: Deleted or moderated posts remain in precomputed timelines until invalidation propagates
expectedIssues.mitigation: Tombstone filtering at read time plus async timeline scrubbing on delete events

expectedIssues.title: Like Counter Row Contention
expectedIssues.description: Like/comment counters on viral posts create row-level lock contention in PostgreSQL
expectedIssues.mitigation: Sharded counters aggregated asynchronously through the event bus; serve approximate counts

expectedIssues.title: Calendar-Event Upload Bursts
expectedIssues.description: New Year's Eve-style events spike uploads 5-10x, saturating the media service and S3 PUT throughput
expectedIssues.mitigation: Pre-scale on known calendar events, client retry with backoff, queue transcoding work

components.label: CDN (Media)
components.costDriver: Media egress — dominant cost at photo/video scale

slaDefinitions.name: Feed Load Latency
slaDefinitions.penalty: Internal SLO — error budget burn freezes feature rollouts

metrics.name: cdn_hit_ratio
metrics.description: CDN cache hit ratio for media

steps: Switch feed-service to degraded chronological DB reads with row limits
Enable per-user recompute throttling to protect the Post DB
Rebuild Redis cluster and warm timelines for top-decile active users
Verify cache hit rate > 80%, then disable degraded mode
Enable origin shield and request coalescing
Raise TTLs on hot media objects
Watch S3 SlowDown (503) rate until it subsides
Escalate to CDN vendor if a POP is degraded
Identify lagging Kafka partitions and confirm leadership is stable
Move highest-follower accounts to pull-based merge
Backfill missed posts from the Post DB once lag drains

decisions.title: Fan-out on Write via Event Bus
decisions.context: Feeds are read orders of magnitude more often than posts are created; feed load latency defines the product
decisions.decision: On post creation, publish an event to Kafka; feed-service consumers precompute follower timelines into Redis
consequences: Feed read is a single cache lookup — O(1) at request time
Write amplification: one post becomes N timeline writes
Freshness is eventually consistent; propagation lag becomes a first-class SLO

decisions.title: CDN-First Media Delivery
decisions.context: Media bytes dwarf API traffic by orders of magnitude; serving them through the app tier would be ruinous
decisions.decision: Clients fetch media directly from the CDN with S3 as origin, fully bypassing the API path
consequences: App tier is sized for metadata, not media bandwidth
CDN hit ratio directly drives both latency and cost
Cache invalidation for moderated media requires CDN purge workflows

decisions.title: Separate Media and Feed Services
decisions.context: Uploads are CPU/IO-heavy and bursty; feed reads are latency-sensitive and constant
decisions.decision: Split media-service (upload/transcode) and feed-service (assembly/fan-out) behind one API gateway
consequences: Each service scales on its own signal (CPU vs consumer lag)
An upload surge cannot degrade feed latency
Two deployment surfaces to operate instead of one

tradeoffs.benefit: Feed loads in one Redis round trip regardless of how many accounts a user follows
tradeoffs.cost: Posts take seconds to minutes to propagate; deletes need tombstone filtering

tradeoffs.choice: Store a copy of each post ID in every follower timeline
tradeoffs.cost: N-times write amplification and large Redis memory footprint, unbounded for celebrity accounts

alternatives.name: Fan-out on Read (Pull Model)
alternatives.description: Assemble feeds at request time by querying recent posts from every followed account
alternatives.prosVsCons: No write amplification, perfectly fresh — but read latency scales with followee count and p99 collapses for users following thousands
alternatives.whyNotChosen: The read path utterly dominates; precomputation moves cost to the cheap async path. Pull is kept only as the celebrity-account fallback

alternatives.name: Media Blobs in the Database
alternatives.description: Store images and video as binary columns alongside post metadata
alternatives.prosVsCons: Transactional consistency between post and media, but PostgreSQL cannot serve petabyte-scale media economically
alternatives.whyNotChosen: S3 + CDN is orders of magnitude cheaper per GB delivered and offloads bandwidth entirely
